title: The Secret Scholarship
premise: Kestrel Oyelaran, a scholarship student and the basketball team's statistician, has survived twelve years of foster care by noticing patterns no one else sees. When his team's group chat begins receiving messages predicting games, injuries, and deaths before they happen — all signed with his late mother's initials — he realizes someone is feeding him a trail toward a truth about her death that the school's powerful benefactors buried. To reach it, Kestrel must keep his team alive through a championship season that is secretly a selection process for something far older than sports. In the end, he wins the game that doesn't matter, loses the one that does by choosing to expose the benefactors rather than join them, and inherits not money but his mother's unfinished work: the memory archive she died protecting.
about_author: Rafael Hartwell is a former high school math teacher who spent six years coaching academic decathlon teams in Ohio before turning to fiction full-time. He writes stories about clever kids in systems designed to break them, and swears every statistic in his books actually checks out.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Being Careful
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We meet him mid-season, cataloguing a rigged free-throw pattern that proves the championship bracket is fixed — and deciding, as always, to say nothing. A flashback to his mother's disappearance twelve years ago establishes his survival rule: notice everything, reveal nothing. Emotional beat: the loneliness of competence.

chapters.title: The Message That Hadn't Happened Yet
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. At 11:47 p.m., the team group chat receives an accurate play-by-play of tomorrow's game — including a career-ending injury to star player Dev that hasn't occurred. Kestrel tries to warn Dev and is dismissed as a superstitious stat nerd. The injury happens exactly as predicted. Emotional beat: dread arriving ahead of its cause.

chapters.title: Initials in the Margins
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Decoding the messages' metadata, Kestrel finds a hidden signature: F.O., his mother Folake Oyelaran's initials. He breaks into the school's locked athletics archive and finds her name on a donor ledger dated three years after her death. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Benefactors
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Kestrel and Coach Adeyemi, who knows more than she says. The school's anonymous benefactors attend the semifinal; their presence makes players perform impossibly well or collapse entirely. Kestrel realizes the tournament is a filter, sorting students into assets and casualties. Emotional beat: the vertigo of seeing the machine.

chapters.title: What Dev Remembers
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. Recovering from his injury, Dev reveals he received predictions too — years ago, as a child, from a woman matching Folake's description at a summer program the benefactors ran. His fragmented memories include a basement, a humming sound, and children reciting future events. Emotional beat: two broken kids comparing scars.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the ledger, Kestrel finds 'The Price List': a document where the benefactors record what each student would sacrifice for their scholarship — and what the school sacrificed for them. His own entry lists his mother. He understands the scholarship was never charity; it was payment. Emotional beat: rage crystallizing into resolve.

chapters.title: Rigged Both Ways
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The benefactors offer Kestrel a deal: win the championship, inherit his mother's seat among them, and learn everything. Refuse, and the predictions continue — next targeting his teammates. Torn, he runs the numbers and finds the only outcome where everyone survives requires losing the real game while winning the fake one. Emotional beat: the weight of a calculated betrayal.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Full-team POV rotation during the final game. Kestrel feeds plays that shouldn't work but do, because he's reverse-engineered the rigging itself. They win gloriously, publicly — buying cover while Kestrel slips away at halftime to the basement beneath the gym. Emotional beat: joy used as camouflage.

chapters.title: The One That Does
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In the humming basement, Kestrel confronts the benefactors and the memory archive — his mother's life's work, recording what the program did to children. Offered the choice to join or be erased, he chooses exposure, triggering the archive's broadcast. The real game was always this room. Emotional beat: courage without any guarantee.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, months later. The school is under investigation; the team scatters but survives; Dev visits weekly. Kestrel finishes digitizing his mother's archive, adding his own entries — careful now not to hide, but to remember out loud. Final image: a new message arrives in the group chat, unsigned, hopeful. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into legacy.
